title: Add initial experimental support for `.webm` video files (VP9)

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body: ## Proposal https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/15617 ## Dependencies Based on #117921 (Add support for `.opus` audio files). ## Overview As discussed in https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/3286#issuecomment-4338452884, re-adding WebM (VP8/VP9) is probably the best bet for adding modern video decoding to Godot (as opposed to Ogg Theora, which is legacy). While there are a number of hurdles that make it hard to implement, it could be a massive improvement to video decoding in Godot: - Better efficiency (smaller files / better quality) - Support for per-pixel transparency, without using a green-screen - Supported by browsers, and commonly used by users (unlike Ogg Theora, which is almost entirely unused & unsupported outside of Godot) - Possible hardware acceleration for much faster decoding - Not necessary to rely on a large & problematically-licensed library like FFmpeg This pull request does not include support for AV1 or AV2. It only supports VP9. Support for VP8 is disabled, as outlined in the proposal. ## Preview As shown above, this pull request allows you to import a VP9 video with Vorbis/Opus audio and play it back successfully. ## Current issues (help needed) 1. ~~Even though it compiles correctly on my machine (using `scons`), it seems to fail in the GitHub Actions due to certain `#include`s not resolving correctly.~~ 2. ~~Certain videos do not seem to play correctly. For example, [this VP8 video](https://test-videos.co.uk/vids/bigbuckbunny/webm/vp8/1080/Big_Buck_Bunny_1080_10s_30MB.webm) consistently plays for a few frames before stopping (although the video time continues to increase, the video appears to freeze). But the [VP9 version](https://test-videos.co.uk/vids/bigbuckbunny/webm/vp9/1080/Big_Buck_Bunny_1080_10s_30MB.webm) of that video plays correctly. I tested the videos in Godot 3.6, and the same issue occurs.~~ 3. Architecture-specific optimisations were intentionally removed in this pull request, because the idea of the pull request is to get a pure-C implementation to a bug-free state before then re-adding architecture-specific optimisations in the future. If added, the architecture-specific optimisations should ideally be optional and not require tools like YASM. 4. Hardware acceleration is outside of the scope of this pull request, but unlike Ogg Theora, there is widespread hardware acceleration support for VP8/VP9. It may be possible to use Vulkan Video to add hardware acceleration. 5. Seeking video is not currently supported. There is a [pull request](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/57744) where someone claims to have added support, but it doesn't work. 6. ~~Transparent video is not currently supported. There is an [open issue](https://github.com/zaps166/libsimplewebm/issues/4) in libsimplewebm to add transparency support, but there is no pull request so far. I've tried to implement it myself, but it appears to be quite complicated - you may need to create a separate VPX decoder for the alpha channel.~~ 7. ~~It's not possible to load a WebM file dynamically yet (must be imported). It should be as simple as adding bindings to the `set_file` function, but I've not tried to do this yet due to the other issues.~~
